In the mathematical subject of [[geometric group theory]], an '''acylindrically hyperbolic group''' is a [[group (mathematics)|group]] admitting a non-elementary 'acylindrical' isometric [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] on some geodesic [[hyperbolic metric space]].<ref name=Osin>{{cite journal |first=D. |last=Osin |title=Acylindrically hyperbolic groups |journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=368 |issue=2 |pages=851–888 |year=2016 |doi=10.1090/tran/6343  |mr=3430352|arxiv=1304.1246 |s2cid=21624534 }}</ref> This notion generalizes the notions of a [[hyperbolic group]] and of a [[relatively hyperbolic group]] and includes a significantly wider class of examples, such as [[mapping class group]]s and [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'')]].

==Formal definition==

===Acylindrical action===

Let ''G'' be a group with an isometric action on some geodesic [[hyperbolic metric space]] ''X''. This action is called '''acylindrical'''<ref name=Osin/> if for every <math>R\ge 0</math> there exist <math> N>0, L>0</math> such that for every <math>x,y\in X</math> with <math>d(x,y)\ge L</math> one has
<math display="block">\# \{g\in G\mid d(x,gx)\le R, d(y,gy)\le R\} \le N.   </math>

If the above property holds for a specific <math>R\ge 0</math>, the action of ''G'' on ''X'' is called ''R''-'''acylindrical'''.  The notion of acylindricity provides a suitable substitute for being a [[proper action]] in the more general context where non-proper actions are allowed. 

An acylindrical isometric action of a group ''G'' on a geodesic [[hyperbolic metric space]] ''X'' is '''non-elementary''' if '''G''' admits two independent [[Hyperbolic_metric_space#The_action_of_isometries_on_the_boundary_and_their_classification|hyperbolic]] isometries of ''X'', that is, two loxodromic elements <math>g,h\in G</math> such that their fixed point sets <math>\{g^+,g^-\}\subseteq \partial X</math> and <math>\{h^+,h^-\}\subseteq \partial X</math> are disjoint. 

It is known (Theorem 1.1 in <ref name=Osin/>) that an acylindrical action of a group ''G'' on a geodesic hyperbolic metric space ''X'' is non-elementary if and only if this action has unbounded orbits in ''X'' and the group ''G'' is not a finite extension of a cyclic group generated by loxodromic isometry of&nbsp;''X''.

===Acylindrically hyperbolic group===

A group ''G'' is called '''acylindrically hyperbolic''' if ''G'' admits a non-elementary acylindrical isometric action on some geodesic hyperbolic metric space&nbsp;''X''.

==Equivalent characterizations== 

It is known (Theorem 1.2 in <ref name=Osin/>) that for a group ''G'' the following conditions are equivalent:

*The group ''G'' is acylindrically hyperbolic.
*There exists a (possibly infinite) generating set ''S'' for ''G'', such that the [[Cayley graph]] <math>\Gamma(G,S)</math> is hyperbolic, and the natural translation action of ''G'' on <math>\Gamma(G,S)</math> is a non-elementary acylindrical action.
*The group ''G'' is not [[virtually cyclic group|virtually cyclic]], and there exists an isometric action of ''G'' on a geodesic hyperbolic metric space ''X'' such that at least one element of ''G'' acts on ''X'' with the WPD ('Weakly Properly Discontinuous') property.
*The group ''G'' contains a proper infinite 'hyperbolically embedded' [[subgroup]].<ref name=DGO>{{cite book |first1=F. |last1=Dahmani |first2=V. |last2=Guirardel |first3=D. |last3=Osin |title=Hyperbolically embedded subgroups and rotating families in groups acting on hyperbolic spaces |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2017 |isbn=978-1-4704-2194-6 |series=[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=245 |id=1156}}</ref>

==History==

==Properties==

*Every acylindrically hyperbolic group ''G'' is [[SQ-universal group|SQ-universal]], that is, every countable group embeds as a subgroup in some [[quotient group]] of ''G''. 
*The class of acylindrically hyperbolic groups is closed under taking infinite [[normal subgroup]]s, and, more generally, under taking 's-normal' subgroups.<ref name=Osin/> Here a subgroup <math>H\le G</math> is called ''s-normal'' in <math>G</math> if for every <math>g\in G</math> one has <math>|H\cap g^{-1}Hg|=\infty</math>. 
*If ''G'' is an acylindrically hyperbolic group and <math>V=\mathbb R</math> or <math>V=\ell^p(G)</math> with <math>p\in [1,\infty)</math> then the [[bounded cohomology]] <math>H_b(G,V)</math> is infinite-dimensional.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Bestvina |first2=K. |last2=Fujiwara |title=Bounded cohomology of subgroups of mapping class groups |journal=[[Geometry & Topology]] |volume=6 |pages=69–89 |year=2002 |arxiv=math/0012115 |doi=10.2140/gt.2002.6.69 | doi-access=free |mr=1914565|s2cid=11350501 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=U. |last=Hamenstädt |title=Bounded cohomology and isometry groups of hyperbolic spaces |journal=[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]] |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=315–349 |year=2008 |doi=10.4171/JEMS/112 | doi-access=free |arxiv=math/0507097|s2cid=16750741 }}</ref><ref name=Osin/>
*Every acylindrically hyperbolic group ''G'' admits a unique maximal normal finite subgroup denoted ''K(G)''.<ref name=DGO/>
*If ''G'' is an acylindrically hyperbolic group with ''K(G)={1}'' then ''G'' has infinite conjugacy classes of nontrivial elements, ''G'' is not inner amenable, and the reduced [[C*-algebra]] of ''G'' is simple with unique trace.<ref name=DGO/>
*There is a version of [[small cancellation theory]] over acylindrically hyperbolic groups, allowing one to produce many quotients of such groups with prescribed properties.<ref>{{cite journal |first=M. |last=Hull |title=Small cancellation in acylindrically hyperbolic groups |journal=[[Groups, Geometry, and Dynamics]] |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=1077–1119 |year=2016 |doi=10.4171/GGD/377 |arxiv=1308.4345|s2cid=118319683 }}</ref>
*Every finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group has cut points in all of its [[asymptotic cone]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |first=A. |last=Sisto |title=Quasi-convexity of hyperbolically embedded subgroups |journal=[[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] |volume=283 |issue=3–4 |pages=649–658 |year=2016 |doi=10.1007/s00209-016-1615-z |arxiv=1310.7753|s2cid=119174222 }}</ref>
*For a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group ''G'', the probability that the [[simple random walk]] on ''G'' of length ''n'' produces a 'generalized loxodromic element' in ''G'' converges to 1 exponentially fast as <math>n\to\infty</math>. <ref>{{cite journal |first=A. |last=Sisto |title=Contracting elements and random walks |journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]] |volume= 2018|issue= 742|pages= 79–114|year= 2018|doi=10.1515/crelle-2015-0093 |arxiv=1112.2666|s2cid=118009555 }}</ref>
*Every finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group ''G'' has exponential conjugacy growth, meaning that the number of distinct [[conjugacy classes]] of elements of ''G'' coming from the ball of radius ''n'' in the [[Cayley graph]] of ''G'' grows exponentially in ''n''. <ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Hull |first2=D. |last2=Osin |title=Conjugacy growth of finitely generated groups |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=235 |issue=1 |pages=361–389 |year=2013 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2012.12.007 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1107.1826}}</ref>

==Examples and non-examples==

*Finite groups, virtually nilpotent groups and virtually solvable groups are not acylindrically hyperbolic.
*Every non-elementary subgroup of a [[word-hyperbolic group]] is acylindrically hyperbolic.
*Every non-elementary [[relatively hyperbolic group]] is acylindrically hyperbolic. 
*The [[mapping class group]] <math>MCG(S_{g,p})</math> of a connected oriented surface of genus <math>g\ge 0</math> with <math>p\ge 0</math> punctures is acylindrically hyperbolic, except for the cases where <math>g=0, p\le 3</math> (in those exceptional cases the mapping class group is finite).<ref name=Osin/>  
*For <math>n\ge 2</math> the group [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'')]] is acylindrically hyperbolic.<ref name=Osin/> 
*By a result of [[Denis Osin|Osin]], every non virtually cyclic group ''G'', that admits a proper isometric action on a proper [[CAT(0) space]] with ''G'' having at least one rank-1 element, is acylindrically hyperbolic.<ref name=Osin/> Caprace and Sageev proved that if ''G'' is a finitely generated group acting isometrically properly discontinuously and cocompactly on a geodetically complete [[CAT(0) space|CAT(0) cubical complex]] ''X'', then either ''X'' splits as a direct product of two unbounded convex subcomplexes, or ''G'' contains a rank-1 element. <ref>
{{cite journal |first1=P.E. |last1=Caprace |first2=M. |last2=Sageev |title=Rank rigidity for CAT(0) cube complexes |journal=[[Geometric and Functional Analysis]] |volume=21 |issue=4 |pages=851–891 |year=2011 |doi=10.1007/s00039-011-0126-7 |arxiv=1005.5687 |mr=2827012|s2cid=119326592 }}</ref> 
*Every right-angled Artin group ''G'', which is not cyclic and which is directly indecomposable, is acylindrically hyperbolic. 
*For <math>n\ge 3</math> the [[special linear group]] <math>SL(n,\mathbb Z)</math> is not acylindrically hyperbolic (Example 7.5 in <ref name=Osin/>).
*For <math>m\ne 0, n\ne 0</math> the [[Baumslag–Solitar group]] <math>BS(m,n)=\langle a,t\mid t^{-1}a^mt=a^n\rangle </math> is not acylindrically hyperbolic. (Example 7.4 in <ref name=Osin/>)
*Many groups admitting nontrivial actions on simplicial trees (that is, admitting nontrivial splittings as fundamental groups of graphs of groups in the sense of [[Bass–Serre theory]]) are acylindrically hyperbolic. For example, all one-relator groups on at least three generators are acylindrically hyperbolic.<ref name=MO>{{cite journal |first1=A. |last1=Minasyan |first2=D. |last2=Osin |title=Acylindrical hyperbolicity of groups acting on trees |journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] |volume=362 |issue=3–4 |pages=1055–1105 |year=2015 |doi=10.1007/s00208-014-1138-z |arxiv=1310.6289|s2cid=55851214 }}</ref>
*Most 3-manifold groups are acylindrically hyperbolic.<ref name=MO/>
